method.pairedChange: Median and range of five per-pair percentages; zero baseline uses absolute changes only.
method.throttleLimit: CDP CPU throttling on Apple M4 Max; not a physical low-power-device result.
method.runnerCleanup: One diagnostic CPU profile produced both rows, then stalled during browser/Vite cleanup. Its owned process group 80243 was terminated. Those rows remain diagnostic and are not a successful acceptance run. The final runner terminates only its own process group on timeout.
method.diagnosticHostContention: Earlier promotion runs had elevated baseline tasks and input-phase duration. External cause was not measured.
method.historicalScreenshotMismatch: The earlier CPU release resized screenshot had a background-only channel delta; form interior pixels matched. That diagnostic result is not part of this new matrix.

fontGuardEvidence.positiveFixture: font-subset-fixture, font-subset-seed, font-subset-covered, font-subset-new-face and font-subset-restored cases exercise the font guard and capture-count assertions.
fontGuardEvidence.limitation: Existing usedCodepoints reads cloned text nodes, not input value attributes. The fresh full-capture oracle also omits a font face used only by new input value glyphs, so this fault cannot establish pixel sensitivity.

diagnostics.status: diagnostic evidence only; not acceptance or a final performance baseline
limitations: Profile stages overlap: snapdomWall includes clone/hook/render wall stages. Do not add overlapping totals.
decodeWall measures image.decode completion; deferred SVG rasterization can execute in a later canvas draw.
Input phase includes automated typing and settling; wall duration varies with main-thread contention and workload completion. Lower task totals can reflect fewer captures or a shorter phase.
One profiled pair and scratch/style pair cannot establish a stable regression or improvement. Profiling and instrumentation perturb timing.

Task-yield and input-promotion are discarded scheduling experiments with two pairs each. Promotion runs exhibit elevated baseline task cost and duration, consistent with host contention; exact external cause was not measured.
Latency decomposition measures event dispatch to capture start, raster wall, composite/publication wall and receipt-to-upload separately. It is not input-to-visible-photon timing.

Largest draw entries are instrumented synchronous drawing stages, not all native draws. Sampled draw stacks separately locate 410.968ms in the region rasterizer and96.561ms in the core source draw; those are sampled totals, not exact per-call durations.

scratchReuseAndStyleDedup.status: single diagnostic pair; same 10 captures and one full capture; snapshot cost decreases, deferred raster/copy still dominates

boundedConclusion: CPU storage shifts substantial raster work from later source upload/draw into region staging and composition. Remaining clone, normalize and deferred raster costs explain why smaller SVG area alone does not guarantee less main-thread work.
GPU6 old-release higher input tails predominantly occur before the acknowledged capture starts; raster, merge and upload distributions are similar. Fewer captures do not prove faster input.

Task-yield lowered frame tails and total tasks while reducing captures 10 to 8, but worsened input tails in all four diagnostic pairs. Input-promotion improved frame tails but raised GPU capture count 10 to 13 and total task time; CPU input tails worsened. Neither experiment establishes a safe improvement.

Scratch/style dedup reduces the measured snapshot cost 96.9 to81.6ms over10 captures, but the single-pair region copy cost rises355.5 to383.7ms and inputp95 is unchanged412.6 to413.4ms. A controlled paired rerun is needed before making a performance claim.
